      "text": "# @everyone We saved the best for last. \n\n# The Finals [Mappool](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1N8kt5ECQft0-e8aZn5zg0FLo_g5t_bJXj1P_A7dNngY/edit?usp\u003dsharing) is@here!\n\n🍺 Thank you for your patience. [The long awaited Finals Mappool is here and finalized in the Spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1N8kt5ECQft0-e8aZn5zg0FLo_g5t_bJXj1P_A7dNngY/edit?usp\u003dsharing).       "text": "Here is my stance: **This announcement is an exceptionally strong piece of community management because it perfectly balances authentic grassroots hype with essential administrative clarity.** \n\nToo often, community tournament hosts make the mistake of trying to sound like overly sterile, corporate esports organizations. Both players on a team are going to have to step up.\n\nHere is a breakdown of why this pool is so well-constructed, along with some thoughts on specific slots:\n\n### 1. The No Mod (NM) Pool: Diverse and Unforgiving\n*   **NM2 (*Ballistic Bunny*):** A nearly 6-minute, 180 BPM stream map is the perfect stamina gatekeeper. It forces players to prove they have the endurance for a Grand Final.\n*   **NM4 (*Sukuinote* - Hakushi Hasegawa):** The note \"Random bullshit go\" is incredibly accurate for Hakushi Hasegawa maps. Having pure avant-garde tech in the NM4 slot will completely expose anyone who relies solely on aim to get through tech maps. \n*   **NM6 (*Seven*):** A 304 BPM 7/8 time signature map is a fantastic rhythm pick. \n\n### 2. Hidden (HD) \u0026 Hard Rock (HR): True to their identities\n*   **The HD Pool:** You didn\u0027t just pick \"NM maps but we put HD on them.\" **HD2 (*Hanakanzashi*)** is an AR8 reading map, which is evil at this level. **HD4 (*4423*)** is a massive gimmick check. This pool demands *actual* HD specialists.\n*   **The HR Pool:** A true test of precision. **HR2 (*Build Our Machine*)** and **HR4 (*Total Eclipse of the Moon*)** are both base CS5. That means with Hard Rock, they become **CS6.5**. That is incredibly demanding on raw aim control and perfectly fits the HR bracket. \n\n### 3. Double Time (DT): Not Just Farm Maps\nI highly respect this DT pool. It\u0027s so easy to just throw four 250 BPM jump maps into DT, but you didn\u0027t.\n*   **DT2 (*Sacrament of Wilderness*):** An old-school OWC pick that requires deep finger control.\n*   **DT4 (*Altitude Remix*):** A base AR7.5 map that turns into AR9.0 with DT, filled with squares. This is a massive reading and awkward-aim check. \n\n### 4. Free Mod (FM) \u0026 EZ: The Draft Breakers\n*   **FM2 (*Dance Away*):** Base CS5.2 and AR7. The note *\"HR is 8* prayge\"* is hilarious. It creates a massive risk/reward dynamic. Do players take the safe route, or do they risk throwing on HR for the multiplier on a map that will become nearly unreadable and microscopic?\n*   **EZ1 (*QUEEN*):** *\"Fuck EZ\"*. Including a mandatory EZ slot in a Grand Finals pool is an incredibly spicy tournament decision. Most high-rank players neglect EZ entirely, meaning this single map could completely swing the momentum of the match if one team has a pocket EZ reader.\n\n### 5. The Tiebreaker (TB)\n*   **TB (*Hatatagami Software*):** A nearly 7-minute, 7.69★, 222 BPM absolute monster. If the match goes to Tiebreaker, the players\u0027 nerves will already be fried. This map will require them to dig deep for every last ounce of stamina they have left. A very fitting \"Final Boss\" map.\n\n### Overall Verdict\nThis is a **10/10 Grand Finals mappool**. It has clearly been thoroughly playtested and thoughtfully assembled (shoutout to the staff you mentioned in the announcement).
